q: Which of the following is NOT necessarily true for a σ-algebra 𝒜?
opts: X ∈ 𝒜 (the whole space is measurable)
If A ∈ 𝒜 then Aᶜ ∈ 𝒜
Countable unions of sets in 𝒜 are in 𝒜
Every subset of a set in 𝒜 is in 𝒜
exp: A σ-algebra is closed under complementation and countable unions, and contains X. But arbitrary subsets of measurable sets need not be measurable — that is what distinguishes measure theory from set theory.
